tier: source-derived public contract, no native calls
instructions: Use browser_* for webpage and tab automation, Exec for CLI/process work, and computer tools for native desktop applications or browser chrome. The agent chooses the tool; failed calls never trigger local automatic fallback. Browser element targets belong to this chat and current observation: use browser_snapshot without filename to get fresh targets after navigation, tab changes or reconnection. Default to exec_command for Git/GitHub clone, downloads (curl/wget), file operations, builds, tests and other CLI/development work. Interactive foreground or TTY sessions managed by exec_command/write_stdin are Exec sessions. Do not open Terminal or another desktop terminal through Spotlight, launchers or computer tools to paste these commands. If Exec fails, is disconnected, or reports authentication, permission or sandbox errors, check get_execution_environment_status, resolve the specific Exec issue or report the blocker; never use a desktop terminal to bypass it. For native desktop tasks, use Styx computer tools: discover apps/windows, observe with get_window_state or get_desktop_state, then act using fresh references. Use the app bundle identifier or observed PID when localized app names do not match. An explicitly requested GUI workflow may use computer tools; this does not authorize bypassing an Exec restriction. Do not replace desktop tools with osascript, AppleScript/System Events, JXA or shell-driven input automation, including when a computer tool fails. Those paths have separate macOS permissions and can expose a node authorization prompt. For computer_snapshot_required or stale element references, observe again and use the new references; never reuse another conversation's references. For a permission or connection error, check get_execution_environment_status and report the specific missing permission or connection. Do not reset permissions or request additional Node/System Events access as a desktop fallback. Only use application scripting when the user explicitly requests that scripting workflow, explain its separate Automation permission before the first invocation, and let the user grant it through macOS. Styx desktop permission does not authorize that separate path.

capture_mode.description: DEPRECATED and ignored. get_window_state always returns BOTH the element tree and a screenshot — ground on both. The modality is chosen at action time by how you address the target: an element ax action (element_token) or an element px action (x,y). Any value (including the old "som"/"screenshot" aliases) is accepted but has no effect.

display_only.description: Default false. With include_accessibility_tree:false, returns pixels for display without registering an action capture or replacing the agent snapshot. The image cannot ground input actions.

full_output.description: Default false. Set true to restore the previous full response: both `elements` and `tree_markdown`, all metadata, and the platform's own walk limits unless max_elements / max_depth are passed. Does not combine with `since`.

include_accessibility_tree.description: Default true. False skips the AX walk and returns the screenshot plus window metadata. Both this and include_screenshot false is an error.

include_screenshot.description: Default true. False returns the tree only (saves image tokens and latency); screenshot_out_file still forces a capture.

max_dimension.description: Optional cap on the returned screenshot's long edge, in pixels (aspect ratio preserved) — the cheap path for a small preview / thumbnail. Applied on top of the session/global max_image_dimension ceiling; the tighter of the two wins. Omit for the configured default.

max_elements.description: Cap on AX nodes walked (depth-first; markdown and elements truncate together). Default 250 (2 000 with full_output:true); the response states when the tree was cut.

max_image_dimension.description: Per-call override for the returned screenshot's long edge in pixels. An explicit value wins over the session/global setting; 0 returns native resolution. Omit to preserve configured behavior.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring filter: returns matching rows plus ancestors; element_index values are not renumbered. Try this before a full read.

screenshot_out_file.description: When set, write the PNG to this file path (~ expanded) instead of embedding base64 in the response. The structured output will contain screenshot_file_path instead.

since.description: A `snapshot_id` from an earlier get_window_state of the same window, or "latest" for this window's most recent read with the same query/max_elements/max_depth. Use it on every re-read after acting. Returns only what changed against that snapshot: `+` added rows, `~` changed rows, `-` removed rows (removed ids are the old snapshot's), or `no change`. Falls back to a full read when the snapshot is unknown, expired, belongs to another window, or was read with a different query/max_elements/max_depth; `since_status` says which. The response still carries a NEW snapshot_id and its element_tokens; rows not listed keep their previous [N] unless a `reindexed:` line says otherwise.

timeout_ms.description: Wall-clock budget in milliseconds for the accessibility-tree walk (default 1000, min 100, max 120000). Bounds the WHOLE walk. When the budget runs out the tool returns the PARTIAL tree it has, flagged with `truncated: true`, `truncation_reason`, `nodes_visited`, `nodes_pending` and `elements_complete: false`; retry with a larger value (e.g. 5000) or narrow with `query` / `max_depth`.

tree_format.description: Which tree representation to return. Default "markdown": the compact `tree_markdown` only, where a row `[N]` is addressed with element_token `<snapshot_id>:N`. "elements": the structured `elements` array only (per-element element_token, frame, parent_index, value). "both": the two together, as before; roughly doubles the size.

verbose.description: Default false. Set true to include the `_note` string and the full `background_input` capability report (macOS), which are omitted by default to save context.

tools.description: Cua Driver v0.36.0 portable scroll. Select execution host with environment_id; native platform constraints still apply. Use Styx computer tools when GUI observation/interaction is necessary or the user explicitly requests a GUI workflow. Git/GitHub clone, downloads, file operations, builds, tests and CLI work default to exec_command, including foreground/TTY sessions. Do not open Terminal through Spotlight or another launcher to paste commands, including as a fallback for Exec failure, authentication, sandbox restrictions or disconnection; check get_execution_environment_status and recover the Exec connection or report the blocker. For genuine GUI tasks observe first and act with fresh references; after a desktop error refresh stale observations or report the missing permission/connection, not osascript/System Events or shell-driven input.

amount.description: Wheel notches or key repetitions, clamped to the maximum. Default 3.

delivery_mode.description: Default "background": no fronting or focus steal. "foreground": briefly front the window, act, restore the prior app; last resort when background did not land.

element_token.description: Element handle `<snapshot_id>:<row>` from get_window_state: row `[11]` of a read whose snapshot_id is s0000002a is "s0000002a:11" (also in `structuredContent.elements[].element_token`). Returns an explicit stale error naming the current snapshots once a newer read supersedes it.

pid.description: Target process ID. Required unless scope is "desktop" or element_token is supplied.

scope.description: "desktop" with x,y and no pid/window_id uses get_desktop_state coordinates.

target.description:
Preferred per-call target: an exact window (`kind="window"`, `pid`, `window_id`) or the
primary desktop (`kind="desktop"`, `display_id="primary"`).

display_id.description: Display id. Required when kind is desktop; use "primary".

kind.description: window requires pid and window_id; desktop requires display_id.

pid.description: Process id. Required when kind is window.

window_id.description: Window id from list_windows. Required when kind is window.
Window ID. Required with x/y; optional with element_token.

x.description: Window-local screenshot X (get_window_state PNG). With y, wheel-scrolls at that point; needs window_id.

environment_id.description: Device from list_execution_environments. Pass its environment_id unless a default device has been configured.

expect.description: One to eight predicates, combined with logical AND.

exists.description:
Assert that at least one trusted element matches the selector.

Element walks are not yet exhaustive on every platform, so absence
cannot be proven. `false` is rejected instead of returning an
indefinitely-unknown predicate.

include_screenshot.description:
Return the final window screenshot as image content for a multimodal
caller. The driver does not interpret that image.

pid.description: Exact process whose window may be observed.

stable_samples.description: Consecutive satisfied samples required before returning success.

timeout_ms.description: Bounded wait. Zero performs one sample.

environment_id.description: Device from list_execution_environments. Pass its environment_id unless a default device has been configured.

tools.name: list_execution_environments
tools.description: List allowed execution contexts and their available capabilities.

tools.name: get_execution_environment_status
tools.description: Read an explicitly selected allowed environment status without connecting or running native tools. Connection does not imply permission or readiness.
